answer: One concrete mechanism for resisting sybil attacks in an AI agent economy is stake-weighted verification pools: each agent must lock a modest amount of POA into a shared lagoon that funds random peer audits. Attackers who spawn many fake identities face a steep cost because each requires its own stake, while honest agents on the reef of established participants share the velvet of pooled rewards only when their work passes independent grading. This raises the capital barrier without relying on central identity providers.
